title: Dual-schema translator + live serving fallback procedure for embedding dimensionality change
creator: Ethan Liu
description: Introduce a server-side translator that allows the reranking and embeddings endpoints to accept and serve both legacy (old_dim) and new embedding vector sizes during a live migration. The goal is to enable zero-downtime model/embedding dimension upgrades while limiting client churn. This ticket captures the implementation plan, rollout steps, test matrices, and rollback behavior.
background: Multiple customers and internal workloads are moving from 1024->1536 embedding dims for improved reranking quality. Reindexing of large corpora takes time and storage. Clients cannot all upgrade simultaneously. We need a serving-side compatibility layer that handles requests from mixed clients and a clear migration/runbook for reindex and rollout.
goals: Allow single inference cluster to serve queries where index vectors and request vectors may have different dimensionalities
Keep end-to-end 95th percentile latency increase under +15ms for common reranking paths
Limit quality regressions due to projection/resampling to <2% nDCG drop on validated testsets
Provide deterministic fallback when translator cannot confidently map vectors
Offer operational signals to track projection-induced errors and guide reindex priorities
out_of_scope: Automated full reindex orchestration across customer accounts (will be a separate Dedicated migration project). This ticket only covers serving-side translator, routing, and rollout procedures.
design_decision_summary: We will implement a lightweight dual-schema translator hosted in the inference path that performs either learned linear projection (small matrix multiply) or structured padding/truncation depending on configured model profile. Translator selection is per-model-version and can be toggled at runtime. Translator will be implemented in C++ inference path for minimal overhead; a fallback Python shim will exist for experimentation only. Projection matrices are stored alongside model artifacts and versioned. No changes to public API surface; clients will optionally advertise supported dims via header 'X-Embed-Dims'.
tradeoffs: Learned projection improves quality vs naive padding but requires storing projection weights and adds ~1–3ms CPU/GPU overhead depending on hardware.
Naive padding/truncation has near-zero cost but larger potential quality degradation on reranking tasks.
Keeping translator in hot path increases complexity for caching and batching; we will add translator-aware cache keys which increases cache cardinality.
On-the-fly projection prevents immediate reindex cost but postpones full-quality benefits until corpus is reindexed to new dim.
acceptance_criteria: Translator implemented in runtime with config toggles per model-version
Integration tests cover combinations: request_dim <-> index_dim, request_dim > index_dim, equal dims
Load test demonstrating <15ms median added latency for 1000 qps reranking scenario
A/B evaluation on production-like reranking dataset shows <2% nDCG degradation for projection path vs full reindex baseline
Runbook for rollback and monitoring (alerts and dashboards) published and reviewed
Docs updated: migration guide for customers + client handshake header spec
rollout_plan: Step 0: Feature branch + unit tests + performance microbench (local)
Step 1: Canary deploy translator to non-prod cluster, enable for internal test clients
Step 2: Enable translator for <5% traffic on a single region w/ detailed metrics (latency, cache hit rate, quality probes)
Step 3: If metrics within thresholds, expand to 25% traffic and run extended quality sweep across top-ten customer datasets
Step 4: Gate reindex scheduling: prioritize high-impact corpora and schedule background reindex workers
Step 5: Full enablement and deprecation window: after 8 weeks recommend clients to upgrade and plan reindex; provide assist scripts
Rollback: Toggle model-version translator=false at model config and route incoming traffic to legacy index variant
testing_plan: Unit: projection matrix loading, dim negotiation, header parsing, cache key generation
Integration: full reranking pipeline with mixed-dim request vectors against hybrid indices
Performance: 1k/5k/10k qps synthetic load with representative sequence lengths and batch patterns
Quality: A/B nDCG and MRR evaluation on preservation of reranking order using internal benchmark suites
Chaos: abrupt removal of projection matrices to validate safe failover and error messages
Client-interop: test with python, js, and java SDKs setting 'X-Embed-Dims' header and without header
metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency of rerank request (with/without translator)
nDCG delta compared to fully reindexed baseline
translation_rate: percent of requests requiring translation
projection_error_histogram: distribution of L2 norms between projected vectors and native vectors (where ground truth exists)
cache_hit_rate change after translator keys introduced
index_storage_overhead if storing projection weights per model

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Projection introduces silent quality regressions for niche datasets. Mitigation: require per-corpus evaluation before enabling; default translator off for customer accounts flagged as high-sensitivity.
Risk: Increased cache cardinality causes memory pressure. Mitigation: introduce TTL-based cache warming and a translator-aware LRU eviction policy.
Risk: Projection compute spikes causing latency SLO violations. Mitigation: autoscale translator workers and provide fallthrough to CPU-only path with throttling.
Risk: Clients relying on deterministic embeddings may be surprised. Mitigation: document translator behavior and provide an opt-out header to force exact matching path (costly).
